sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: December 11, 2025 announcement explicitly makes GPT-5.2 Thinking available that day in ChatGPT and the API as gpt-5.2, separately from Instant/chat-latest and Pro. Documents reasoning, tool use, vision and cached inputs; no numerical model parameter counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.2 API model documentation
sources.evidence: Direct current Markdown binds gpt-5.2 to gpt-5.2-2025-12-11; gives 400,000 context and 128,000 maximum output, text/image inputs, text output, reasoning tokens, none/low/medium/high/xhigh effort, function calling, file uploads, prompt caching and Responses/Chat Completions. No deprecated or shut-down status is shown.

sources.title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Downloaded original December 11, 2025 PDF; searched full text and inspected training and exact Thinking passages. Separates thinking and instant variants, describes reinforcement-learning reasoning training and evaluations. Does not disclose total/active counts or detailed block/expert structure.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Directly fetched technical guide expressly applies to models before GPT-5.6. Explains OpenAI caching through Transformer attention key/value projections and names gpt-5.2 in its model table. Exact-model caching support plus this mechanism permits a qualified broad Transformer inference.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Directly fetched guide specifies Responses PDF processing into text and page images for vision-capable models; Chat Completions also accepts PDF file content. Supports PDF as an API format, not a separate native model modality.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.4
sources.evidence: March 5, 2026 successor announcement contains exact GPT-5.2 comparison columns across professional work, coding, vision, tools, long context and reasoning. These are benchmark results, not parameter counts or detailed structural disclosures.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card
sources.evidence: Later March 5, 2026 card explicitly identifies GPT-5.2 Thinking as its predecessor baseline. Exact gpt-5.2-thinking columns in safety comparisons and model-specific monitorability discussion disclose behavior, not production parameter counts or architecture. Later model training details are not transferred.

sources.title: Reasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought
sources.evidence: Downloaded full PDF and inspected exact GPT-5.2 experiments and parameter-related passages. Evaluates GPT-5.2 reasoning/control behavior. The parameter-size study concerns open-weight GPT-OSS and Qwen; RL scaling intervention uses Olmo. Those numbers do not describe GPT-5.2.

sources.title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2 — updated online card
sources.evidence: Current card includes later GPT-5.2 Thinking CoT monitorability and controllability analyses. Its training and model-specific research discussion does not publish parameter counts or detailed network structure.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: Directly fetched complete deprecation list. No exact gpt-5.2 or gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 shutdown notice found at review. GPT-5.2 Chat and Codex have distinct notices that do not apply to this Thinking API record. This is documentation evidence, not an endpoint test.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Section 9.1 reserves service IP rights and grants limited use rather than ownership. Used as descriptive proprietary hosted-service classification, not a named downloadable-weight license or an assertion about exact launch-day contract wording.

sources.title: All OpenAI API models
sources.evidence: Direct current catalog lists GPT-5.2 as a previous flagship, without the shutdown labels applied to Chat and Codex. Separately identifies Apache-2.0 open-weight gpt-oss releases; no GPT-5.2 weight distribution is offered.

sources.title: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL
sources.evidence: May 7, 2026 training-research lead inspected. It identifies GPT-5.2 Instant among affected models, not this GPT-5.2 Thinking API variant. Its variant-specific training statements are not transferred; it supplies no Thinking parameter count or architecture.

name.note: Official API name; launch explicitly identifies this alias with GPT-5.2 Thinking.

developer.note: Developer identified by the first-party release and authored system card.

family.note: GPT-5.2 release family, within the wider GPT-5 series; distinct from Instant, Pro and Codex variants.

release_date.note: Dated original announcement explicitly releases Thinking in ChatGPT and the API that day; does not rely solely on the snapshot suffix.

open_weights.note: Documented distribution is hosted ChatGPT/API access under retained service rights; the publisher separately identifies its downloadable open-weight models.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted model, not an SPDX checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: No exact total count disclosed in the reviewed original, later comparison or first-party research sources. Open-weight experiment sizes, performance scores and sibling specifications are not GPT-5.2 weights.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active count or dense/MoE routing specification found for this exact Thinking variant. Reasoning effort is inference compute, not an activated-weight count.

architecture.note: Qualified cross-source operational inference: exact GPT-5.2 supports prompt_caching and the applicable technical guide names it while explaining Transformer-layer attention KV tensors. This does not establish exclusively Transformer blocks, a complete layer inventory, dense/MoE routing, dimensions or parameter counts.

context_window.note: Exact API documentation gives 400,000 context separately from 128,000 maximum output. No input maximum is stated; none is derived by subtraction or borrowed from ChatGPT product limits.

modalities.note: Native inputs are text/image and output is text. PDF denotes supported API preprocessing into text and page images for this vision/file-upload model; tool-generated images and video benchmarks do not establish native image/video output.

reasoning.note: Explicit Thinking identity and reasoning-token support. Configurable effort includes none (default), low, medium, high and xhigh; default none does not mean the model lacks reasoning support.

tool_call.note: Exact API documentation explicitly supports function calling and Responses tools.

description.value: GPT-5.2 reasoning model with text and image input, function calling and a 400,000-token context window.

patch.notes: The gpt-5.2 API alias maps to GPT-5.2 Thinking and documents default snapshot gpt-5.2-2025-12-11, distinct from Instant/chat-latest, Pro and Codex. Context is 400,000 tokens with a separate 128,000 maximum output; no maximum input is stated on the exact model page. Reasoning effort supports none (default), low, medium, high and xhigh. PDF denotes API extraction into text and page images. Transformer is a qualified operational inference from exact prompt-caching support and the applicable Transformer attention KV mechanism; complete block design, dense/MoE routing and total/active counts remain undisclosed in the checked sources. As of October 27, 2026, the exact API model page has no deprecated/shut-down designation and the reviewed deprecation list has no shutdown notice for this alias or dated snapshot; Chat and Codex retirement notices are separate. No endpoint test was made.

summary: Confirmed December 11, 2025 Thinking/API release, 400K context, configurable reasoning and tool calling. Corrected family, descriptive license, PDF API format, qualified broad Transformer inference and factual description. Total/active parameters remain undisclosed after original and later exact-model comparison/training research. Distinguishes this API model from retired Chat/Codex siblings without claiming tested endpoint availability.
